body:
# the contributor audit: projective weighted facet residual credit

Source: `candidate 4283399302c56a21`.

Result: PASS as a local arbitrary-facet inequality and an explicitly
compatible two-input deformation. No integrated Gamma/2 payment is proved.

The tangent continuation satisfies f^(-1/d)=t on its inverse-power
branch and delta(d+1-dt/delta)^(-1/d) below it. Its derivative increases
to1 at the join and is1 above, so the required inverse-root convexity
is global. There is no hidden positive-denominator assumption on input
faces lying outside the original source body.

I checked the cited ordinary BBL statement directly in Lemma2.3 of
[Bobkov's paper](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~bobko001/papers/2010_PTRF_Norms.pdf).
In tangent dimension k=d-1, the density exponent-1/d integrates to-1.
The statement requires no symmetry. Restricting the three continuous
positive densities to their actual bounded midpoint sets meets its
measurability and integrability hypotheses. Open residual sets are
legitimate; zero input mass gives the trivial zero lower bound.

Parallel-plane offsets are consistent: after orthonormal tangent
identification, each actual midpoint and the equality c_A+c_B=2y
give the precise affine-argument midpoint required for inverse-root
convexity. There is no missing slope-dependent Hausdorff Jacobian.
The captured and missed midpoint inclusions use the SAME original
ambient cap with its integer tilt. At a whole-face coincidence the
inward bit is obtained by positive transverse shifts whose speeds
average to the middle speed. Continuity of the weights and dominated
convergence then give the correct limit; closed face mass is not
substituted for lost volume. Finite intersections of captured or missed
caps satisfy the same inclusion, so the joint-event assertion is valid.

The scalar credit formula follows by maximizing total missed mass S.
For a<=b and S>b, the smallest possible missed product is b(S-b),
attained by filling the larger endpoint's missed capacity first.
Solving 2b(S-b)/S<=R gives S<=2b^2/(2b-R), hence credit
a-Rb/(2b-R) below the harmonic threshold. Its denominator is positive
there; the formula joins zero at the threshold. The displayed equality
data prove scalar sharpness only, exactly as stated.

The actual two-input fields both use the SAME source support H(n) and
the specified shifted density. Ordinary convexity of f gives their
averaged speed at least the target speed. Support averaging then
proves exact midpoint containment in the source gauge erosion. Interior
input centers are not needed, since the fields are globally finite,
positive and bounded on compact neighborhoods. The established normal
first-variation theorem therefore gives the stated actual facet costs
and losses. The separate one-input fields have different arguments and
coefficients; the source correctly prohibits inserting their costs in
this residual formula without a new proof.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
